CSCI3100 Software Engineering

Introduction

Target: Learn how to blow water on the theory of software development.

Software Development Processes

Plan-and-Development: specification -> design -> implementation -> verification -> maintanence

Agile Manifesto: speed up life-cycles + respond to change + test-driven development (TDD + autotest) + behaviour-driven development (BDD + user stories)

Testing: quality assurance (QA), verification (match spec?) + validation (spec good?), unit (single method) -> module (group of methods) -> integration (communication between modules) -> system (meets its program spec)

Productivity: clarity (conciseness) + synthesis (gen code by code) + DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) + automation (use tools)

Software-as-a-Service (SaaS): Sell software instead of hardware, leading to rise of service-oriented architecture (SOA) and microservices (e.g. cloud computing or webpages)

Learning Languages and Frameworks

Steps: Type -> Primitive -> Method -> Class -> Symbols -> Library -> Debugging -> Testing

Ruby is weak-typing, everything is an object (without multiple inheritance, only nil and false are falsy), where function calls are simply sending signals to the receiver. Sometimes {} and () are optional.

class A < B (inheritance); @balance (instance variable); @@bank (class variable); balance (instance method); self.bank (class method); attr_accessor: (R+W) / attr_reader: (R) / attr_writer: (W)

Hashs: {:a => 1, :b => "two"}, :a are enumerables, f-string "Answer is #{@foo}" or %Q{Answer is #{@foo + 1}}

Lists: x.sort (include Comparable; def <=>), x.reverse! (modifies), x.filter do |f| f.includes?("e") end, x.any? { |f| f.length > 5 }; yield and iterator

Library: gem, require "abc" then bundle install, specified in Gemfile (Gemfile.lock)

Software-as-a-Service (SaaS)

Client-Server Pattern: a server responds to many clients; Peer-to-Peer Architecture: everyone serves as client and server

Domain Name System (DNS) maps names to IP addresses; Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is stateless (thus rely on cookie) and bases on TCP/IP protocols; Web 2.0 involves the introduction of javascript (Asynchonous JavaScript - AJAX and XmlHttpRequest).

RESTful API (REpresentational State Transfer): Represent requests to action on resources, which JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) are often used.

Sinatra: path /:user/account -> params[]; Views: .erb; erb :view; cookies: session[]

Model-View-Controller (MVC) Framework - Rails

The MVC Framework consists of models, views and controllers:

  1. Model: how data are stored and manipulated (CRUD)
  2. View: how to display data for users to interact
  3. Controller: generate actions in front-end and handled back-end

Rails's MVC: models/*.rb <-> controllers/*.rb (MoveController#show) <-> views/[action].html.erb. Routes: get '/movie/:id', debug(@movie)

RESTful routes: New (GET) + Create (POST), Read (GET), Edit (GET) + Update (PUT/PATCH), Delete (DELETE)

Database: ApplicationRecord, Movie.where("rating = :rating", rating: 'PG'); new, save, save! (exception), build (for foreign key), create (new + save), update, destroy; Foreign key: has_many, belongs_to, through; scope for lambdas

Validation (on model): validate :function, validates :name, presence: true, valid?; Filters (on controller): before_action :function_name; Shared templates (on views): <%= render "form", moviegoer: @moviegoer %>

Single Sign On (SSO): Third party login

Behaviour-Driven Design (BDD)

Cucumber: focus on user story (behaviour) to verify if execute correctly over implementation

Feature: story name; Scenario: path; describe: context; Given [condition] When [do something] Then [check condition] And [condition] But [condition]

Capybara: visit; click_link; fill_in "xxx", :with => "yyy"; select "xxx" form "yyy"; click_button "xxx"; .find (with selenium)

Declarative Scenario: Given /I have added "(.*)" with rating "(.*)"/ do |title, rating|

Test-Driven Development (TDD)

RSpec: [precondition] act [assert]. expect(x).to eq('Ruby'); expect(res).to render_template("movies/search"); allow, double. Method stub

Design Pattern

  1. Single Responsibility Principle: Do one thing only
  2. Open/Closed Principle: Open for extension, closed for modification
  3. Liskov Substitution Principle: Subtype can substitute base type
  4. Injecting Dependency: create abstraction to reduce source modification
  5. Demeter Principle: minimally expose yourself
